_readme: External hosts the Bash egress guard (scripts/hooks/bash-egress-guard.py) treats as legitimate.
Localhost is ALWAYS allowed and is not listed here -- it is a built-in rule, not a grant.
A host matches itself and its subdomains: 'example.com' also allows 'api.example.com'.
Re-read on every hook invocation: adding a host takes effect immediately, no restart, no deploy.
A missing or malformed file means NO grants (localhost only). Losing this file can never widen
what is permitted -- it only removes grants, which is the safe direction to fail in.
Seeded from the 854182c7 corpus measurement (2,928,984 Bash commands): every host below was
observed in real fleet traffic with an identifiable purpose. Hosts that appeared in the corpus
but whose purpose was not identifiable were deliberately NOT seeded -- the log will show them
if they are still in use, and an operator can grant them on evidence rather than on my guess.
pypi.org and api.anthropic.com are Peti's 2026-10-09 approval (Telegram 10704, card 18055f83)
of backend3's 2026-09-29 log analysis (store/bash-egress.log, 307 lines, card 18055f83 comment
9023): the only real non-selftest external traffic the log showed before enforce was armed --
pip version checks and our own Anthropic API usage probe.
CORRECTION 2026-10-09 (Peti decision, Telegram 10715, card 18055f83 comment 13319, RedHat
MEDIUM-1): cloudflare-dns.com and dns.google were REMOVED again, same day they were added.
A DoH resolver answers arbitrary query names, so granting it is effectively an open DNS
channel -- whatever name a hijacked agent resolves through it reaches that name's own
authoritative server, defeating the point of an allowlist. They are not re-added here; if DoH
traffic is needed again, it needs its own narrower design (e.g. fixed query names), not a
blanket grant of the resolver.
